segments.arabic: [140] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم قال: أخبرنا أبو سلمة الخزاعي منصور بن سلمة قال: أخبرنا ابن بلال يعني سليمان عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن ابن عباس
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim related to us. He said: Abu Salamah al-Khuza‘i, Mansur ibn Salamah, informed us. He said: Ibn Bilal—meaning Sulayman—informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

segments.arabic: أنه توضأ فغسل وجهه ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فمضمض بها واستنشق ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فجعل بها هكذا أضافها إلى يده الأخرى فغسل بهما وجهه ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فغسل بها يده اليمنى ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فغسل بها يده اليسرى ثم مسح برأسه ثم أخذ غرفة من ماء فرش على رجله اليمنى حتى غسلها ثم أخذ غرفة أخرى فغسل بها رجله يعني اليسرى، ثم قال هكذا رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ
segments.english: He performed ablution and washed his face. Then he took a handful of water and rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose with it. Then he took a handful of water and did this with it: he added it to his other hand and washed his face with both. Then he took a handful of water and washed his right hand and arm with it. Then he took a handful of water and washed his left hand and arm with it. Then he wiped his head. Then he took a handful of water and sprinkled it on his right foot until he had washed it. Then he took another handful and washed his foot with it—meaning the left. Then he said: “This is how I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”

notes: The full chain includes Abu Salamah’s identifying name and “Ibn Bilal—meaning Sulayman”. The historical print uses a different reporting verb before Abu Salamah; the selected digital and modern-print “informed us” is retained.

The opening face-washing statement and the subsequent described sequence remain in their selected order. The repeated handfuls, right/left sides, joining the other hand, sprinkling until washed and final “meaning the left” remain. No elbow/ankle limits or explanation of blowing water out is inserted into this report where the selected wording does not state them.

segments.arabic: [141] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن سالم بن أبي الجعد عن كريب عن ابن عباس يبلغ به النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Kurayb, from Ibn ‘Abbas, attributing it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: لو أن أحدكم إذا أتى أهله قال بسم الله اللهم جنبنا الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا فقضي بينهما ولد لم يضره
segments.english: “If one of you, when he comes to his wife, says: ‘In the name of Allah. O Allah, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You grant us,’ and a child is decreed for them, he would not harm him.”

notes: The full chain and Ibn ‘Abbas’s attribution to the Prophet remain. The invocation retains both requests and “what You grant us”; the conditional decree of a child and final pronouns remain.

The comparison’s added instruction about exactly when the invocation must be said and its explanatory “coming offspring” parentheses are not inserted into the selected wording. This is a translation of the report, not added legal guidance.

segments.arabic: [142] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عبد العزيز بن صهيب قال: سمعت أنسا يقول
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb, who said: I heard Anas saying:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا دخل الخلاء قال اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الخبث والخبائث
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the privy, he would say: “O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female devils.”

segments.arabic: تابعه بن عرعرة عن شعبة، وقال غندر عن شعبة إذا أتى الخلاء، وقال موسى عن حماد إذا دخل، وقال سعيد بن زيد حدثنا عبد العزيز إذا أراد أن يدخل
segments.english: Ibn ‘Ar‘arah followed him in transmitting this from Shu‘bah. Ghundar said, from Shu‘bah: “When he came to the privy.” Musa said, from Hammad: “When he entered.” Sa‘id ibn Zayd said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us: “When he wanted to enter.”

notes: All four following transmission attributions and the variants “entered”, “came” and “wanted to enter” remain. The main report is not silently replaced by the final variant. Sa‘id’s “related to us” remains in the closing note.

“Male and female devils” is the provisional rendering of الخبث والخبائث, reading khubuth as in the vocalised prints. The English comparison families use different renderings; the Encyclopedia of Translated Prophetic Hadiths also records an alternative understanding as evil and impurities (https://hadeethenc.com/en/browse/hadith/3150). This lexical choice still needs independent review. The Khan-family body omits the following transmission variants.

segments.arabic: [143] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا هاشم بن القاسم قال: حدثنا ورقاء عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد عن ابن عباس
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us. He said: Warqa’ related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, from Ibn ‘Abbas:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ دخل الخلاء فوضعت له وضوءا قال من وضع هذا فأخبر، فقال اللهم فقهه في الدين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the privy, and I set out water for his ablution. He said: “Who put this here?” He was told, and he said: “O Allah, give him understanding of the religion.”

notes: The full chain, Ibn ‘Abbas’s first-person placement of the water, the question, the passive “he was told” and the invocation remain. “Understanding of the religion” renders فقهه في الدين without adding a named qualification or legal office.

segments.arabic: [144] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب قال: حدثنا الزهري عن عطاء بن يزيد الليثي عن أبي أيوب الأنصارى قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us. He said: Al-Zuhri related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid al-Laythi, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا أتى أحدكم الغائط فلا يستقبل القبلة ولا يولها ظهره شرقوا أو غربوا
segments.english: “When one of you goes to relieve himself, he should neither face the qiblah nor turn his back towards it. Face east or west.”

notes: The selected wording retains both prohibitions and the direct plural instruction “Face east or west.” No geographical explanation or legal qualification is inserted into the report. The source chapter heading remains separate from the numbered report.
The selected chain has “from ‘Ata’”; the historical print has “that ‘Ata’”. The selected wording is retained.

segments.arabic: [145] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان عن عمه واسع بن حبان عن عبد الله بن عمر أنه كان يقول
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from his uncle Wasi‘ ibn Habban, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, who used to say:

segments.arabic: إن ناسا يقولون إذا قعدت على حاجتك فلا تستقبل القبلة ولا بيت المقدس، فقال عبد الله بن عمر لقد ارتقيت يوما على ظهر بيت لنا فرأيت رسول الله ﷺ على لبنتين مستقبلا بيت المقدس لحاجته، وقال لعلك من الذين يصلون على أوراكهم فقلت لا أدري والله
segments.english: Some people say: “When you sit down to relieve yourself, do not face the qiblah or Jerusalem.” ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said: “One day I climbed onto the roof of a house of ours and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on two bricks, facing Jerusalem to relieve himself.” He said: “Perhaps you are among those who pray on their hips.” I said: “I do not know, by Allah.”

segments.arabic: قال: مالك يعني الذي يصلي ولا يرتفع عن الأرض يسجد وهو لاصق بالأرض
segments.english: Malik said: He means someone who prays without raising himself from the ground, prostrating while pressed against the ground.

notes: The report retains the earlier claim, Ibn ‘Umar’s roof observation, the two bricks, the direction, the following question and reply, and Malik’s full closing explanation. The final first-person reply is not silently rewritten to name its speaker.

The Khan-family body stops after the roof account and adds a screen explanation and a commentary citation; these additions are not inserted. Its absent question, reply and Malik note are checked against the selected Arabic, both prints and the Bewley comparison. “Hips” is a provisional rendering of أوراكهم; the attached explanation remains.

arabicCorrections.englishRendering: You have been permitted to go out

contextNotes.label: A recorded spelling correction
contextNotes.text: Both Arabic prints spell the permission verb أذن; the digital paragraph spells it إذن. This prototype records that one-letter spelling change and keeps the original in source notes. Independent review is pending.

segments.arabic: [146] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث قال: حدثنا عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us. He said: ‘Uqayl related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن أزواج النبي ﷺ كن يخرجن بالليل إذا تبرزن إلى المناصع وهو صعيد أفيح فكان عمر يقول للنبي ﷺ احجب نساءك فلم يكن رسول الله ﷺ يفعل فخرجت سودة بنت زمعة زوج النبي ﷺ ليلة من الليالي عشاء وكانت امرأة طويلة فناداها عمر ألا قد عرفناك يا سودة حرصا على أن ينزل الحجاب فأنزل الله آية الحجاب
segments.english: The wives of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to go out at night to relieve themselves at al-Manasi‘, a broad open plain. ‘Umar used to say to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Veil your wives,” but the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not do so. One evening, Sawdah bint Zam‘ah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out. She was a tall woman. ‘Umar called to her: “Indeed, we have recognised you, Sawdah!” He was eager for the hijab to be revealed, so Allah revealed the verse of hijab.

segments.arabic: وحدثنا زكريا قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: And Zakariyya related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: قد أذن أن تخرجن في حاجتكن
segments.english: “You have been permitted to go out for your needs.”

segments.arabic: قال هشام يعني البراز
segments.english: Hisham said: He means relieving oneself.

comparisons.note: The selected entry contains two narrations. The Khan-family EPUB numbers their report bodies separately as 148 and 149; the first corresponds to segments 1–2, the second to segments 3–5. Its abbreviated chains and omitted closing explanation do not independently verify those complete segments.

notes: The selected entry contains two complete narrations with separate chains. They correspond to modern Arabic print 146 and 147, Bewley 146, and Khan-family 1.4.148 and 1.4.149. Both chains and Hisham’s closing explanation are retained; segment-to-comparison ownership is explicitly recorded. The English comparisons abbreviate the chains.

Both printed second narrations read أذن; the digital paragraph reads إذن. Only that hamza spelling is corrected in the derived Arabic, visibly recorded with the original unchanged. The English renders the passive permission; it does not treat إذن as the separate word “then”.

The historical print has “related to us” from ‘Uqayl, as selected; the modern print has “related to me”. The historical first narration ends “Allah revealed the hijab”, while the selected digital and modern print include “the verse of hijab”. These differences are not harmonised.

The place, evening, Sawdah’s description, plural “we have recognised”, ‘Umar’s eagerness and the revelation statement remain. Modern geographical and clothing explanations in the Khan-family parentheses are not inserted. “Veil” and the retained term “hijab” are provisional renderings, not added rulings.

segments.arabic: [147] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا أنس بن عياض عن عبيد الله عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان عن واسع بن حبان عن عبد الله بن عمر قال
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Anas ibn ‘Iyad related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, from Wasi‘ ibn Habban, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

segments.arabic: ارتقيت فوق ظهر بيت حفصة لبعض حاجتي فرأيت رسول الله ﷺ يقضي حاجته مستدبر القبلة مستقبل الشام
segments.english: I climbed onto the roof of Hafsah’s house for a need of mine, and I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, relieving himself with his back towards the qiblah, facing al-Sham.

notes: The need belonging to Ibn ‘Umar, Hafsah’s roof, both directions and the full chain remain. Al-Sham is retained as a historical place name; no list of modern countries is inserted.

segments.arabic: [148] حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا يزيد بن هارون قال: أخبرنا يحيى عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان أن عمه واسع بن حبان أخبره أن عبد الله بن عمر أخبره قال
segments.english: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Harun related to us. He said: Yahya informed us, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban, that his uncle Wasi‘ ibn Habban informed him that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar informed him, saying:

segments.arabic: لقد ظهرت ذات يوم على ظهر بيتنا فرأيت رسول الله ﷺ قاعدا على لبنتين مستقبل بيت المقدس
segments.english: One day I went up onto the roof of our house and saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sitting on two bricks, facing Jerusalem.

notes: The chain preserves the two “informed him” links and the distinct “informed us” verb. The account remains separate from 145 and 147, including the two bricks and Jerusalem. No omitted action is supplied from a parallel report.

segments.arabic:
[149] حدثنا أبو الوليد هشام بن عبد الملك قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي معاذ واسمه عطاء بن أبي ميمونة قال:
سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Mu‘adh, whose name is ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ إذا خرج لحاجته أجيء أنا وغلام معنا إداوة من ماء
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, a boy and I would come with a small water vessel.

segments.arabic: يعني يستنجي به
segments.english: Meaning: he would cleanse himself with it.

notes: The complete selected single paragraph is divided only for display into chain, report and closing explanation. Abu Mu‘adh’s identifying name and Anas’s hearing remain. The explanation “Meaning: he would cleanse himself with it” is retained without inventing a named speaker; the Khan-family comparison attributes it to Hisham.

A small water vessel renders إداوة من ماء. No claim about its being a modern tumbler or about its exact capacity is added. The digital and both Arabic prints say “the Prophet”; the Khan-family comparison says “Allah’s Apostle”.

segments.arabic: [150] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي معاذ هو عطاء بن أبي ميمونة قال: سمعت أنسا يقول
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu Mu‘adh—he is ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah—who said: I heard Anas saying:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا خرج لحاجته تبعته أنا وغلام منا معنا إداوة من ماء
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, a boy from among us and I followed him, carrying a small water vessel.

notes: The identifying chain phrase “Abu Mu‘adh—he is ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah” and “a boy from among us” remain. The separate Abu al-Darda’ chapter introduction is not merged into this report or its daily-session audio script.

The historical print names ‘Ata’ directly without the Abu Mu‘adh identification and has “the Prophet”; the selected digital and modern print retain the fuller identification and “the Messenger of Allah”.

segments.arabic: [151] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا محمد بن جعفر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن عطاء بن أبي ميمونة سمع أنس بن مالك يقول
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Maymunah, who heard Anas ibn Malik saying:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يدخل الخلاء فأحمل أنا وغلام إداوة من ماء وعنزة يستنجي بالماء
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would enter the privy, and a boy and I would carry a small water vessel and an ‘anazah. He would cleanse himself with the water.

segments.arabic: تابعه النضر وشاذان عن شعبة العنزة عصا عليه زج
segments.english: Al-Nadr and Shadhan followed him in transmitting this from Shu‘bah. An ‘anazah is a staff with an iron tip.

notes: The full chain, two carriers, water vessel, ‘anazah, use of water, two corroborating transmitters and closing definition all remain. The selected source’s definition is rendered “a staff with an iron tip”; the word زج is not expanded into an asserted use of the staff.
The Khan-family body does not include the closing corroboration and definition. Those are retained from the selected Arabic and compared with both prints and Bewley.

segments.arabic: [152] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام هو الدستوائي عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham—he is al-Dastawa’i—related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: قال رسول الله ﷺ: إذا شرب أحدكم فلا يتنفس في الإناء وإذا أتى الخلاء فلا يمس ذكره بيمينه ولا يتمسح بيمينه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you drinks, he should not breathe into the vessel. When he goes to the privy, he should not touch his penis with his right hand or wipe himself with his right hand.”

notes: Both printed chains and the selected Arabic name ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah from his father. The Bewley web introduction says Abu Qatada from his father; that shortened or defective name is not substituted. Hisham’s identification as al-Dastawa’i remains.

The three prohibitions remain in their selected order, including the drinking condition and both occurrences of “with his right hand”. The explicit anatomical word renders ذكره without extending it to other body parts.

segments.arabic: [153] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الأوزاعي عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Al-Awza‘i related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا بال أحدكم فلا يأخذن ذكره بيمينه ولا يستنج بيمينه ولا يتنفس في الإناء
segments.english: “When one of you urinates, he must not hold his penis with his right hand, cleanse himself with his right hand, or breathe into the vessel.”

notes: The full chain remains, including ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah from his father, notwithstanding the different shortened chain in the Bewley web introduction.

The selected and historical chain says “related to us” from al-Awza‘i, while the modern print says “related to me”. The selected form is retained. The emphatic prohibition in فلا يأخذن, both right-hand references and the final vessel clause remain. This report remains distinct from 152.

segments.arabic: [154] حدثنا أحمد بن محمد المكي قال: حدثنا عمرو بن يحيى بن سعيد بن عمرو المكي عن جده عن أبي هريرة قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Makki related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya ibn Sa‘id ibn ‘Amr al-Makki related to us, from his grandfather, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: اتبعت النبي ﷺ وخرج لحاجته فكان لا يلتفت فدنوت منه، فقال ابغني أحجارا أستنفض بها
segments.english: I followed the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he went out to relieve himself. He did not turn around. I drew near to him, and he said: “Find me stones with which to cleanse myself.”

segments.arabic: أو نحوه
segments.english: Or words to that effect.

segments.arabic: ولا تأتني بعظم ولا روث فأتيته بأحجار بطرف ثيابي فوضعتها إلى جنبه وأعرضت عنه فلما قضى أتبعه بهن
segments.english: “And do not bring me a bone or dung.” I brought him stones in the edge of my garments, placed them beside him and turned away from him. When he had finished, he used them.

notes: The complete selected chain retains both occurrences of ‘Amr. The historical print reads عمير in the second ancestral name, whereas the selected digital and modern print read عمرو. The selected ‘Amr is retained; the difference is recorded without claiming a resolved biographical identification.

The narrator’s uncertainty “or words to that effect” remains at its original position between the request for stones and the prohibition of bone or dung. It is a separate transmission-note segment without deleting it from reading or narration.

The report retains not turning around, drawing near, the edge of the garments, placing the stones beside him and turning away. The final clause is rendered “he used them” with its reference to the stones; the defective final phrase in the Bewley web comparison is not copied.

segments.arabic: [155] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا زهير عن أبي إسحاق قال ليس أبو عبيدة ذكره ولكن عبد الرحمن بن الأسود عن أبيه أنه سمع عبد الله يقول
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: It was not Abu ‘Ubaydah who mentioned it, but ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, that he heard ‘Abdullah saying:

segments.arabic: أتى النبي ﷺ الغائط فأمرني أن آتيه بثلاثة أحجار فوجدت حجرين والتمست الثالث فلم أجده فأخذت روثة فأتيته بها فأخذ الحجرين وألقى الروثة، وقال هذا ركس
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to relieve himself and ordered me to bring him three stones. I found two stones and looked for the third, but could not find it. I took a piece of dung and brought it to him. He took the two stones, threw away the dung, and said: “This is unclean.”

segments.arabic: وقال إبراهيم بن يوسف عن أبيه عن أبي إسحاق حدثني عبد الرحمن
segments.english: And Ibrahim ibn Yusuf said, from his father, from Abu Ishaq: ‘Abd al-Rahman related to me.

contextNotes.label: Material supplied from Arabic prints

witnesses.differenceNote: The historical print includes قال before the final reporting verb and prints إسحق, أبى and حدثنى. The selected modern reading omits that قال and uses إسحاق, أبي and حدثني. These readings are retained separately; they are not silently harmonised.

notes: The chain explicitly rejects Abu ‘Ubaydah as the transmitter here and names ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad from his father. That correction within the source wording is retained, along with the father’s hearing of ‘Abdullah. No personal name absent from the chain is inserted.

The search for the third stone, the two found stones, the dung, its rejection and the final description remain. “Unclean” is a working rendering of ركس. The comparison translations add “dried”; the selected Arabic does not, so that adjective is not inserted.

The modern Arabic print labels this report 156. segments.arabic: [156] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: توضأ النبي ﷺ مرة مرة
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, washing each part once.

notes: Both printed witnesses and both English comparisons retain washing once for each part. The repetition مرة مرة is rendered distributively, without adding a rule about how often one must wash. The full selected chain remains visible and narrated.

segments.arabic: [157] حدثنا حسين بن عيسى قال: حدثنا يونس بن محمد قال: حدثنا فليح بن سليمان عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر ابن عمرو بن حزم عن عباد بن تميم عن عبد الله بن زيد
segments.english: Husayn ibn ‘Isa related to us. He said: Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Fulayh ibn Sulayman related to us, from ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm, from ‘Abbad ibn Tamim, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ توضأ مرتين مرتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, washing each part twice.

notes: The selected and modern print have Fulayh introduced with حدثنا and the name ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn ‘Amr ibn Hazm. The historical print uses أخبرنا before Fulayh and includes Muhammad in the longer ancestral name. The selected digital wording is retained; these are recorded witness differences, not silently merged chains.

segments.arabic: [158] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله الأويسي قال: حدثني إبراهيم بن سعد عن ابن شهاب أن عطاء بن يزيد أخبره أن حمران مولى عثمان أخبره
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abdullah al-Uwaysi related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to me, from Ibn Shihab, that ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid informed him that Humran, the freedman of ‘Uthman, informed him:

segments.arabic: أنه رأى عثمان بن عفان دعا بإناء فأفرغ على كفيه ثلاث مرار فغسلهما ثم أدخل يمينه في الإناء فمضمض واستنشق ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثا ويديه إلى المرفقين ثلاث مرار ثم مسح برأسه ثم غسل رجليه ثلاث مرار إلى الكعبين، ثم قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: من توضأ نحو وضوئي هذا ثم صلى ركعتين لا يحدث فيهما نفسه غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: He saw ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan call for a vessel. He poured over his palms three times and washed them. Then he put his right hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth and drew water into his nose. Then he washed his face three times and his hands up to the elbows three times. Then he wiped his head, and then washed his feet up to the ankles three times. Then he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak‘ahs without letting his thoughts wander during them, will have his past sins forgiven.”

segments.arabic: وعن إبراهيم قال: قال صالح بن كيسان قال ابن شهاب ولكن عروة يحدث عن حمران
segments.english: And from Ibrahim, who said: Salih ibn Kaysan said: Ibn Shihab said: But ‘Urwah relates from Humran:

segments.arabic: فلما توضأ عثمان قال ألا أحدثكم حديثا لولا آية ما حدثتكموه سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: لا يتوضأ رجل يحسن وضوءه ويصلي الصلاة إلا غفر له ما بينه وبين الصلاة حتى يصليها
segments.english: When ‘Uthman performed ablution, he said: “Shall I relate to you a hadith which, were it not for a verse, I would not have related to you? I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saying: ‘A man who performs ablution, does it well and offers the prayer will be forgiven for what occurs between that and the [next] prayer, until he offers it.’”

segments.arabic: قال عروة الآية { إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات }
segments.english: ‘Urwah said: The verse is: “Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs.”

notes: Both linked narrations, their chains, the second introductory question and ‘Urwah’s closing verse identification remain in source order. Modern print numbers the two narrations 159 and 160; the selected digital entry and Khan-family 1.4.161 contain both.

The self-talk idiom لا يحدث فيهما نفسه is rendered as not letting his thoughts wander, consistent with both English body comparisons. The first account says the right hand enters the vessel, then mouth rinsing and drawing water into the nose. It does not separately say blowing water out, whereas 162 does; the extra action in the English comparisons is not inserted here. The Arabic hands-to-elbows expression is retained rather than adding a separate limb list.

The second prayer clause uses [next] as an explicitly supplied English word. Both English comparisons understand the interval as extending to the next prayer; the Arabic commentary at https://dorar.net/hadith/sharh/3834 explains that reading using parallel narrations. The selected Arabic does not itself say “next”, and remains unchanged. Compulsory and congregational specifications from the Khan-family comparison are not inserted. This translation choice still needs independent review.

The selected and modern print quote the verse through من البينات. The historical print ends its quoted fragment at ما أنزلنا. The selected longer fragment remains, with no completion of the rest of the Quranic verse.

segments.arabic: [159] حدثنا عبدان قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا يونس عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أبو إدريس أنه سمع أبا هريرة عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Idris informed me that he heard Abu Hurayrah relate from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

segments.arabic: من توضأ فليستنثر ومن استجمر فليوتر
segments.english: “Whoever performs ablution should blow water out of his nose, and whoever cleanses himself with stones should use an odd number.”

contextNotes.label: An incomplete English comparison
contextNotes.text: The checked Bewley web entry omits the final clause about an odd number of stones. This draft keeps that clause from the selected Arabic, both printed witnesses and the other English comparison.

notes: The full concluding clause about an odd number of cleansing stones is present in the selected digital text, both inspected prints and Khan-family 1.4.162. It is absent from the checked Bewley 159 web body. That partial comparison is not treated as proof of completeness. Both clauses remain in the working English and complete narration.
The separate chapter introduction naming ‘Uthman, ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd and Ibn ‘Abbas stays in chapter browsing. It is never added to this hadith or narration script.

segments.arabic: [١٦٢] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا توضأ أحدكم فليجعل في أنفه ثم لينثر ومن استجمر فليوتر وإذا استيقظ أحدكم من نومه فليغسل يده قبل أن يدخلها في وضوئه فإن أحدكم لا يدري أين باتت يده
segments.english: “When one of you performs ablution, he should put [water] into his nose and then blow it out. Whoever cleanses himself with stones should use an odd number. When one of you wakes from his sleep, he should wash his hand before putting it into his ablution water, for none of you knows where his hand spent the night.”

notes: The selected chain begins with the exact Arabic-digit label [١٦٢]. Its reader number 160 is an explicit body/reference match, not a replacement of the source numeral. The later digital [162] is a separate report and remains reader 162.

The historical print explicitly has ماء after “into his nose”; the selected digital and modern print leave the object implicit. The working English marks the supplied object as [water], without changing the Arabic. Singular hand is retained in both waking clauses.

The literal === delimiters in the original source are retained as formatting spans. Only the exact heading words form the separate chapter heading; the whole original paragraph is available in the source notes.

segments.arabic: [161] حدثنا موسى قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة عن أبي بشر عن يوسف بن ماهك عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال
segments.english: Musa related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf ibn Mahak, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said:

segments.arabic: تخلف النبي ﷺ عنا في سفرة سافرناها فأدركنا وقد أرهقنا العصر فجعلنا نتوضأ ونمسح على أرجلنا فنادى بأعلى صوته ويل للأعقاب من النار مرتين أو ثلاثا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stayed behind us on a journey we were making. He caught up with us when the time for ‘Asr was pressing upon us. We began performing ablution and wiping over our feet. He called out at the top of his voice: “Woe to the heels from the Fire!” Two or three times.

notes: The warning remains twice or three times, preserving the narrator’s alternative. The wording about wiping over the feet is retained; parenthetical legal explanations from the English comparisons are not inserted.
The historical print abbreviates the journey clause; the selected and modern print retain “on a journey we were making.” The selected fuller phrase remains.

segments.arabic: [162] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عطاء بن يزيد عن حمران مولى عثمان بن عفان
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ata’ ibn Yazid informed me, from Humran, the freedman of ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan:

segments.arabic: أنه رأى عثمان دعا بوضوء فأفرغ على يديه من إنائه فغسلهما ثلاث مرات ثم أدخل يمينه في الوضوء ثم تمضمض واستنشق واستنثر ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثا ويديه إلى المرفقين ثلاثا ثم مسح برأسه ثم غسل كل رجل ثلاثا، ثم قال: رأيت النبي ﷺ يتوضأ نحو وضوئي هذا، وقال من توضأ نحو وضوئي هذا ثم صلى ركعتين لا يحدث فيهما نفسه غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه
segments.english: He saw ‘Uthman call for water for ablution. He poured from his vessel over his hands and washed them three times. Then he put his right hand into the ablution water, rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose and blew it out. Then he washed his face three times and his hands up to the elbows three times. Then he wiped his head and then washed each foot three times. Then he said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution like this ablution of mine, and he said: ‘Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then prays two rak‘ahs without letting his thoughts wander during them, Allah will forgive his past sins.’”

notes: The complete water sequence explicitly includes rinsing the mouth, drawing water into the nose and expelling it, followed by face, hands to elbows, head and each foot. The singular each-foot wording and the named subject Allah in the forgiveness clause remain.

This is the later digital label [162], distinct from the earlier Arabic-digit [١٦٢] assigned reader 160. Its references are independently matched: modern print 164, Bewley 162 and Khan-family 1.4.165.

segments.arabic: [163] حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا محمد بن زياد قال: سمعت أبا هريرة وكان يمر بنا والناس يتوضؤون من المطهرة قال
segments.english: Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ziyad related to us. He said: I heard Abu Hurayrah—he would pass by us while the people were performing ablution from the water vessel—say:

segments.arabic: أسبغوا الوضوء فإن أبا القاسم ﷺ قال ويل للأعقاب من النار
segments.english: “Perform ablution thoroughly, for Abu al-Qasim, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Woe to the heels from the Fire!’”

notes: Muhammad ibn Ziyad’s hearing of Abu Hurayrah and the setting at the water vessel remain in the full introduction. Abu al-Qasim remains the name used in the source; no explanatory replacement is inserted.
The Ibn Sirin statement about washing the ring area is separate chapter context and remains outside this report and narration.

segments.arabic: [164] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن سعيد المقبري عن عبيد بن جريج أنه قال لعبد الله بن عمر
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Sa‘id al-Maqburi, from ‘Ubayd ibn Jurayj, that he said to ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: يا أبا عبد الرحمن رأيتك تصنع أربعا لم أر أحدا من أصحابك يصنعها قال وما هي يا ابن جريج قال: رأيتك لا تمس من الأركان إلا اليمانيين ورأيتك تلبس النعال السبتية ورأيتك تصبغ بالصفرة ورأيتك إذا كنت بمكة أهل الناس إذا رأوا الهلال ولم تهل أنت حتى كان يوم التروية
segments.english: “Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, I have seen you do four things which I have not seen any of your companions do.” He said: “What are they, Ibn Jurayj?” He said: “I have seen you touch none of the corners except the two Yemeni ones. I have seen you wear tanned-leather sandals, and I have seen you dye with yellow. I have seen that, when you are in Makkah, the people begin the talbiyah when they see the crescent, but you do not begin it until the Day of Tarwiyah.”

segments.arabic: قال عبد الله أما الأركان فإني لم أر رسول الله ﷺ يمس إلا اليمانيين وأما النعال السبتية فإني رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يلبس النعل التي ليس فيها شعر ويتوضأ فيها فأنا أحب أن ألبسها وأما الصفرة فإني رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يصبغ بها فأنا أحب أن أصبغ بها وأما الإهلال فإني لم أر رسول الله ﷺ يهل حتى تنبعث به راحلته
segments.english: ‘Abdullah said: “As for the corners, I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, touch any except the two Yemeni ones. As for tanned-leather sandals, I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, wear sandals with no hair on them and perform ablution while wearing them, so I like to wear them. As for the yellow, I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dye with it, so I like to dye with it. As for beginning the talbiyah, I did not see the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, begin it until his mount rose with him.”

notes: All four observations, the question asking what they are and all four answers remain in order. The two Yemeni corners, hairless sandals, yellow dye, crescent and Day of Tarwiyah are retained.

The selected Arabic does not state a hair object for dyeing or name henna; the working English does not import those additions from the comparisons. It also preserves the mount rising with him, without replacing it with a date or a journey-to-Hajj explanation. Ihlal is rendered as beginning the talbiyah.

segments.arabic: [166] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني أشعث بن سليم قال: سمعت أبي عن مسروق عن عائشة قالت

segments.arabic: [167] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك أنه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ وحانت صلاة العصر فالتمس الناس الوضوء فلم يجدوه فأتي رسول الله ﷺ بوضوء فوضع رسول الله ﷺ في ذلك الإناء يده وأمر الناس أن يتوضؤوا منه قال: فرأيت الماء ينبع من تحت أصابعه حتى توضؤوا من عند آخرهم
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the time for the ‘Asr prayer had come. The people looked for water for ablution but did not find any. Water for ablution was brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, put his hand into that vessel and ordered the people to perform ablution from it. He said: I saw water springing from beneath his fingers until every last one of them had performed ablution.

notes: The repeated references to the Messenger of Allah, the arrival of ‘Asr, unsuccessful search, brought water, hand in the vessel, instruction to the people and every last person finishing are all retained. No explanatory miracle label is added to the hadith.

The historical print begins with “I saw the Prophet,” while the selected and modern print say “I saw the Messenger of Allah.” The selected wording remains. The chapter’s separate ‘A’ishah statement about missing dawn water and tayammum is not part of this narration.

segments.arabic: [169] حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحيم قال: أخبرنا سعيد بن سليمان قال: حدثنا عباد عن ابن عون عن ابن سيرين عن أنس

segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: [171] حدثنا إسحاق أخبرنا عبد الصمد حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن دينار سمعت أبي عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ

segments.arabic: أن رجلا رأى كلبا يأكل الثرى من العطش فأخذ الرجل خفه فجعل يغرف له به حتى أرواه فشكر الله له فأدخله الجنة
segments.english: A man saw a dog eating damp earth out of thirst. The man took his leather sock and began scooping [water] for it with it, until he had quenched its thirst. Allah appreciated his deed and admitted him to Paradise.

segments.arabic: [173] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة عن ابن أبي السفر عن الشعبي عن عدي بن حاتم قال:
segments.english: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Ibn Abi al-Safar, from al-Sha‘bi, from ‘Adi ibn Hatim, who said:

segments.arabic: سألت النبي ﷺ، فقال إذا أرسلت كلبك المعلم فقتل فكل وإذا أكل فلا تأكل فإنما أمسكه على نفسه قلت: أرسل كلبي فأجد معه كلبا آخر قال: فلا تأكل فإنما سميت على كلبك ولم تسم على كلب آخر
segments.english: I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “If you send your trained dog and it kills, then eat. If it eats, do not eat, for it has caught it for itself.” I said: “I send my dog and find another dog with it.” He said: “Then do not eat, for you invoked the name over your dog and did not invoke the name over another dog.”

notes: The two conditions about the trained dog, the question about a second dog, and the distinction between the names invoked over them are retained. The Arabic does not explicitly repeat Allah as the object of سميت; the working English retains “invoked the name” rather than silently expanding it. The explanatory hunting question supplied by the English comparisons is not inserted.

segments.arabic: قال النبي ﷺ لا يزال العبد في صلاة ما كان في المسجد ينتظر الصلاة ما لم يحدث، فقال رجل أعجمي ما الحدث يا أبا هريرة قال الصوت

segments.arabic: [177] حدثنا سعد بن حفص حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة أن عطاء بن يسار أخبره أن زيد بن خالد أخبره أنه سأل عثمان بن عفان رضى الله تعالى عنه قلت:
segments.english: Sa‘d ibn Hafs related to us. Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, that ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar informed him that Zayd ibn Khalid informed him that he asked ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, may Allah Most High be pleased with him. I said:

segments.arabic: أرأيت إذا جامع فلم يمن قال عثمان يتوضأ كما يتوضأ للصلاة ويغسل ذكره قال عثمان سمعته من رسول الله ﷺ فسألت عن ذلك عليا والزبير وطلحة وأبي بن كعب رضى الله تعالى عنهم فأمروه بذلك
segments.english: “What do you think if he has intercourse but does not ejaculate?” ‘Uthman said: “He performs ablution as he does for prayer and washes his penis.” ‘Uthman said: “I heard it from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” I asked ‘Ali, al-Zubayr, Talhah and Ubayy ibn Ka‘b, may Allah Most High be pleased with them, about that, and they instructed him to do that.

segments.arabic: [178] حدثنا إسحاق قال: أخبرنا النضر قال: أخبرنا شعبة عن الحكم عن ذكوان أبي صالح عن أبي سعيد الخدري

segments.arabic: [179] حدثني محمد بن سلام قال: أخبرنا يزيد بن هارون عن يحيى عن موسى بن عقبة عن كريب مولى ابن عباس عن أسامة بن زيد
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Salam related to me. He said: Yazid ibn Harun informed us, from Yahya, from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Usamah ibn Zayd:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ لما أفاض من عرفة عدل إلى الشعب فقضى حاجته قال أسامة بن زيد فجعلت أصب عليه ويتوضأ فقلت: يا رسول الله أتصلي، فقال المصلى أمامك
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, departed from ‘Arafah, he turned aside into the mountain pass and relieved himself. Usamah ibn Zayd said: I began pouring for him while he performed ablution. I said: “Messenger of Allah, will you pray?” He said: “The place of prayer is ahead of you.”

notes: The single Arabic paragraph is divided at its exact chain/report boundary for presentation, with no lost or reordered character. The selected opening is حدثني (related to me), while the historical print uses حدثنا. The selected and modern print name Muhammad ibn Salam; the historical print uses Ibn Salam without Muhammad.

The mountain pass, relieving himself, Usamah pouring, the question about prayer and the answer remain. The Khan-family location explanation “in Al-Muzdalifa” is absent from this selected Arabic and is not inserted.

segments.arabic: [180] حدثنا عمرو بن علي قال: حدثنا عبد الوهاب قال: سمعت يحيى بن سعيد قال: أخبرني سعد بن إبراهيم أن نافع بن جبير بن مطعم أخبره أنه سمع عروة بن المغيرة بن شعبة يحدث عن المغيرة بن شعبة
segments.english: ‘Amr ibn ‘Ali related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id say: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed me that Nafi‘ ibn Jubayr ibn Mut‘im informed him that he heard ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah relating from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah:

segments.arabic: أنه كان مع رسول الله ﷺ في سفر وأنه ذهب لحاجة له وأن مغيرة جعل يصب الماء عليه وهو يتوضأ فغسل وجهه ويديه ومسح برأسه ومسح على الخفين
segments.english: He was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. He went to attend to a need of his, and al-Mughirah began pouring water for him while he performed ablution. He washed his face and hands, wiped his head and wiped over the two leather socks.

notes: The exact single-paragraph source is divided into chain and report without changing the stored Arabic. Nafi‘ informing Sa‘d, his hearing of ‘Urwah and ‘Urwah relating from al-Mughirah remain explicit.

The selected report preserves its indefinite “a need of his,” hands, head and both leather socks. The English comparisons explain the need and use forearms; those expansions are not imported into the chosen wording.

segments.arabic: [181] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن مخرمة بن سليمان عن كريب مولى ابن عباس أن عبد الله بن عباس أخبره
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

segments.arabic: أنه بات ليلة عند ميمونة زوج النبي ﷺ وهي خالته فاضطجعت في عرض الوسادة واضطجع رسول الله ﷺ وأهله في طولها فنام رسول الله ﷺ حتى إذا انتصف الليل أو قبله بقليل أو بعده بقليل استيقظ رسول الله ﷺ فجلس يمسح النوم عن وجهه بيده ثم قرأ العشر الآيات الخواتم من سورة آل عمران ثم قام إلى شن معلقة فتوضأ منها فأحسن وضوءه ثم قام يصلي
segments.english: He spent a night with Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who was his maternal aunt. I lay across the cushion, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, slept until the middle of the night, or a little before it, or a little after it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, woke up and sat wiping the sleep from his face with his hand. Then he recited the last ten verses of Surat Al ‘Imran. Then he went to a hanging worn waterskin and performed ablution from it, doing his ablution well. Then he stood to pray.

segments.arabic: قال ابن عباس فقمت فصنعت مثل ما صنع ثم ذهبت فقمت إلى جنبه فوضع يده اليمنى على رأسي وأخذ بأذني اليمنى يفتلها فصلى ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم أوتر ثم اضطجع حتى أتاه المؤذن فقام فصلى ركعتين خفيفتين ثم خرج فصلى الصبح
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas said: I got up and did as he had done. Then I went and stood beside him. He placed his right hand on my head and took my right ear, twisting it. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs, then two rak‘ahs. Then he performed witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He rose and prayed two light rak‘ahs, then went out and prayed the dawn prayer.

notes: The source changes from a third-person introduction to “I lay”; that change is preserved. The cushion (وسادة), singular “his hand,” timing alternatives, old waterskin and six separately stated pairs of rak‘ahs remain. Witr is named without adding a number that this Arabic does not state. The word أهله is rendered his wife in this context, as in both English comparisons.
The two statements preceding the report remain one separate Arabic chapter-introduction block. No ruling or greeting instruction is inserted into the hadith.

segments.arabic: [182] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن امرأته فاطمة عن جدتها أسماء بنت أبي بكر أنها قالت
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his wife Fatimah, from her grandmother Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, who said:

segments.arabic: أتيت عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ حين خسفت الشمس فإذا الناس قيام يصلون وإذا هي قائمة تصلي فقلت: ما للناس فأشارت بيدها نحو السماء وقالت سبحان الله فقلت: آية فأشارت أي نعم فقمت حتى تجلاني الغشي وجعلت أصب فوق رأسي ماء فلما انصرف رسول الله ﷺ حمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال: ما من شيء كنت لم أره إلا قد رأيته في مقامي هذا حتى الجنة والنار ولقد أوحي إلي أنكم تفتنون في القبور مثل أو قريبا من فتنة الدجال
segments.english: I came to ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The people were standing in prayer, and she was standing in prayer. I said: “What is happening with the people?” She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “A sign?” She indicated: yes. I stood until faintness overtook me, and I began pouring water over my head. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he praised Allah and extolled Him. Then he said: “There is nothing I had not previously seen but that I saw it while standing here, even Paradise and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves with a trial like—or close to—the trial of the false messiah.

segments.arabic: لا أدري أي ذلك قالت أسماء
segments.english: I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

segments.arabic: يؤتى أحدكم فيقال ما علمك بهذا الرجل فأما المؤمن أو الموقن
segments.english: One of you will be approached and asked: ‘What do you know of this man?’ As for the believer—or the one who is certain—

segments.arabic: لا أدري أي ذلك قالت أسماء
segments.english: I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

segments.arabic: فيقول هو محمد رسول الله جاءنا بالبينات والهدى فأجبنا وآمنا واتبعنا فيقال نم صالحا فقد علمنا إن كنت لمؤمنا وأما المنافق أو المرتاب
segments.english: he will say: ‘He is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah. He brought us clear proofs and guidance, and we responded, believed and followed.’ It will be said: ‘Sleep, righteous one; we have known that you were indeed a believer.’ As for the hypocrite—or the one who doubts—

segments.arabic: لا أدري أي ذلك قالت أسماء
segments.english: I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

segments.arabic: فيقول لا أدري سمعت الناس يقولون شيئا فقلته
segments.english: he will say: ‘I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.’”

notes: All three narrator uncertainty statements remain at their exact source positions, including the first after the false-messiah comparison. They are transmission notes, not words attributed to the Prophet. The Khan-family comparison explicitly keeps only the first uncertainty; its other shortened wording does not replace the complete selected text.

The selected chain says Fatimah and her grandmother. The historical print supplies her patronymic bint al-Mundhir and a direct reporting verb before Asma’; the selected and modern print have the shorter name and link. The selected reading is unchanged.

Faintness is retained without adding a separate recovery event. The selected passive “one of you will be approached” does not name angels; the Khan-family explanation is not inserted. This form does not include the threefold repetition of Muhammad found in selected 86.

segments.arabic: [183] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن عمرو بن يحيى المازني عن أبيه
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا قال لعبد الله بن زيد وهو جد عمرو بن يحيى أتستطيع أن تريني كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يتوضأ، فقال عبد الله بن زيد نعم فدعا بماء فأفرغ على يديه فغسل مرتين ثم مضمض واستنثر ثلاثا ثم غسل وجهه ثلاثا ثم غسل يديه مرتين مرتين إلى المرفقين ثم مسح رأسه بيديه فأقبل بهما وأدبر بدأ بمقدم رأسه حتى ذهب بهما إلى قفاه ثم ردهما إلى المكان الذي بدأ منه ثم غسل رجليه
segments.english: A man said to ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd, who was the grandfather of ‘Amr ibn Yahya: “Can you show me how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution?” ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd said: “Yes.” He called for water, poured it over his hands and washed twice. Then he rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose three times. Then he washed his face three times. Then he washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he wiped his head with both hands, moving them forward and back. He began at the front of his head, took them to his nape, then returned them to the place where he had begun. Then he washed his feet.

notes: The relationship “grandfather of ‘Amr ibn Yahya” is present in the selected source and both prints and is retained without a genealogical correction. The singular/plural movements and all wash counts are retained. The final feet clause does not explicitly say ankles; the Khan-family parenthesis is not inserted.

The source says washed twice without an expressed object in that clause; the hands remain clear from the preceding clause. Its nasal action is expelled water, while the English comparisons expand the inhaling step. The chosen wording remains concise. The separate chapter introduction remains in Arabic.

segments.arabic: [184] حدثنا موسى قال: حدثنا وهيب عن عمرو عن أبيه
segments.english: Musa related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from ‘Amr, from his father:

segments.arabic: شهدت عمرو بن أبي حسن
segments.english: I witnessed ‘Amr ibn Abi Hasan

segments.arabic: سأل عبد الله بن زيد عن وضوء النبي ﷺ فدعا بتور من ماء فتوضأ لهم وضوء النبي ﷺ فأكفأ على يده من التور فغسل يديه ثلاثا ثم أدخل يده في التور فمضمض واستنشق واستنثر ثلاث غرفات ثم أدخل يده فغسل وجهه ثلاثا ثم غسل يديه مرتين إلى المرفقين ثم أدخل يده فمسح رأسه فأقبل بهما وأدبر مرة واحدة ثم غسل رجليه إلى الكعبين
segments.english: asking ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He called for a basin of water and performed the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, for them. He tipped water from the basin onto his hand and washed his hands three times. Then he put his hand into the basin, rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose and expelled it, using three handfuls. Then he put his hand in and washed his face three times. Then he washed his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he put his hand in and wiped his head, moving both hands forward and back once. Then he washed his feet up to the ankles.

notes: The selected first source paragraph ends after the name ‘Amr ibn Abi Hasan; the second continues with his question. The exact paragraph boundary remains, and presentation retains the complete sentence across both blocks. The full mouth-rinsing, nasal actions, three handfuls, each count and once-only head wiping remain.

A basin is named without supplying an earthenware material. The selected and printed source say his hand in the singular when dipping; the plural forms in parts of the English comparisons are not silently substituted.

segments.arabic: [185] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا الحكم قال: سمعت أبا جحيفة يقول
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Al-Hakam related to us. He said: I heard Abu Juhayfah say:

segments.arabic: خرج علينا رسول الله ﷺ بالهاجرة فأتي بوضوء فتوضأ فجعل الناس يأخذون من فضل وضوئه فيتمسحون به فصلى النبي ﷺ الظهر ركعتين والعصر ركعتين وبين يديه عنزة،
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out to us in the midday heat. Water for ablution was brought to him and he performed ablution. The people began taking the remaining water from his ablution and wiping themselves with it. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak‘ahs for Zuhr and two rak‘ahs for ‘Asr, with a short spear in front of him.

segments.arabic: وقال أبو موسى دعا النبي ﷺ بقدح فيه ماء فغسل يديه ووجهه فيه ومج فيه، ثم قال لهما اشربا منه وأفرغا على وجوهكما ونحوركما
segments.english: And Abu Musa said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a cup containing water. He washed his hands and face in it and expelled water from his mouth into it. Then he said to the two of them: “Drink from it and pour it over your faces and upper chests.”

notes: Abu Juhayfah’s report and the following statement introduced by Abu Musa both remain complete and in order. The modern print numbers these separately as 187 and 188; the selected digital report and English comparison 1.4.187 group them. Neither part is dropped or given a new app identity.

The historical print uses an indirect link before al-Hakam whereas the selected and modern print use حدثنا. The selected report says Messenger of Allah where the historical print says Prophet. Those selected forms remain. The names of the two people and explanations about a prayer barrier are not supplied from the Khan-family brackets.

segments.arabic: [186] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم بن سعد قال: حدثنا أبي عن صالح عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع قال
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: My father related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ informed me. He said:

segments.arabic: وهو الذي مج رسول الله ﷺ في وجهه وهو غلام من بئرهم،
segments.english: He was the one into whose face the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, expelled water from his mouth when he was a boy, from their well.

segments.arabic: وقال عروة عن المسور وغيره يصدق كل واحد منهما صاحبه وإذا توضأ النبي ﷺ كادوا يقتتلون على وضوئه
segments.english: And ‘Urwah related from al-Miswar and another, each confirming the other: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, they nearly fought over the water from his ablution.

notes: The full opening chain, the biographical clause about Mahmud, and the following ‘Urwah statement remain separate blocks in one selected report. The indefinite other transmitter and reciprocal confirmation remain. No unnamed people are silently replaced with an explicit “Companions” label.

Water is made explicit as the object of the mouth action in English, supported by the source’s well phrase and both comparisons; the selected Arabic remains unchanged. The child’s statement is not combined into the ‘Urwah transmission as in the condensed Khan-family sentence.

segments.arabic: [187] حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن يونس قال: حدثنا حاتم بن إسماعيل عن الجعد قال: سمعت السائب بن يزيد يقول
segments.english: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Hatim ibn Isma‘il related to us, from al-Ja‘d, who said: I heard al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid say:

segments.arabic: ذهبت بي خالتي إلى النبي ﷺ فقالت: يا رسول الله ان ابن أختي وجع فمسح رأسي ودعا لي بالبركة ثم توضأ فشربت من وضوئه ثم قمت خلف ظهره فنظرت إلى خاتم النبوة بين كتفيه مثل زر الحجلة
segments.english: My maternal aunt took me to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, my sister’s son is ill.” He wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me. Then he performed ablution, and I drank from the water of his ablution. Then I stood behind his back and looked at the seal of prophethood between his shoulders, like a zirr al-hajalah.

contextNotes.label: A phrase awaiting English review
contextNotes.text: The final phrase zirr al-hajalah is kept in transliteration. The comparison translations give different explanations; its English rendering remains unresolved. The Arabic wording and comparison notes are available in the source details.

notes: The selected source says ill (وجع), without specifying the legs; both English comparisons add a leg condition. That additional detail is not imported. The source heading is only باب; the reader title remains simply Chapter rather than an invented topic.

The final comparison زر الحجلة has differing English renderings: the Bewley comparison gives a partridge egg; the Khan-family comparison retains a transliteration and lists alternative explanations. This draft retains zirr al-hajalah in transliteration. Its English meaning is unresolved here and requires independent review; it is not silently fixed to one interpretation. Both printed Arabic witnesses retain the selected phrase.

segments.arabic: [188] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا خالد بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا عمرو بن يحيى عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن زيد
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Khalid ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to us, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd:

segments.arabic: أنه أفرغ من الإناء على يديه فغسلهما ثم غسل أو مضمض واستنشق من كف واحدة ففعل ذلك ثلاثا فغسل يديه إلى المرفقين مرتين مرتين ومسح برأسه ما أقبل وما أدبر وغسل رجليه إلى الكعبين، ثم قال هكذا وضوء رسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: He poured water from the vessel onto his hands and washed them. Then he washed—or rinsed his mouth—and drew water into his nose from one palmful. He did that three times. He washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice, wiped his head forward and back, and washed his feet up to the ankles. Then he said: “This is the ablution of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: The wording alternative غسل أو مضمض is retained rather than silently selecting mouth-rinsing alone as in the Khan-family comparison. The single palmful, three repetitions, twice for each arm, both directions of head wiping and ankles are retained.
This selected form has no explicit face-washing clause or nasal expulsion verb. Those steps from neighbouring reports are not inserted into this report. It remains separate from 183, 184 and 189.

segments.arabic: [189] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا وهيب قال: حدثنا عمرو بن يحيى عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to us, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: شهدت عمرو بن أبي حسن سأل عبد الله بن زيد عن وضوء النبي ﷺ فدعا بتور من ماء فتوضأ لهم فكفأ على يديه فغسلهما ثلاثا ثم أدخل يده في الإناء فمضمض واستنشق واستنثر ثلاثا بثلاث غرفات من ماء ثم أدخل يده في الإناء فغسل وجهه ثلاثا ثم أدخل يده في الإناء فغسل يديه إلى المرفقين مرتين مرتين ثم أدخل يده في الإناء فمسح برأسه فأقبل بيديه وأدبر بهما ثم أدخل يده في الإناء فغسل رجليه
segments.english: I witnessed ‘Amr ibn Abi Hasan asking ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd about the ablution of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He called for a basin of water and performed ablution for them. He tipped water onto his hands and washed them three times. Then he put his hand into the vessel, rinsed his mouth, drew water into his nose and expelled it three times with three handfuls of water. Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed his face three times. Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he put his hand into the vessel and wiped his head, moving his hands forward and back. Then he put his hand into the vessel and washed his feet.

segments.arabic: وحدثنا موسى قال: حدثنا وهيب قال مسح رأسه مرة
segments.english: And Musa related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: He wiped his head once.

notes: Every repeated dipping action remains explicit. The closing Musa–Wuhayb transmission is present in the Arabic and Bewley; the main Khan-family body 1.4.191 omits it. EPUB 1.4.192 begins a separate Wuhayb continuation but is truncated before its action is complete. That incomplete item is not counted as a complete matching statement.

The historical print says Messenger of Allah in the question and includes a different opening form; the selected and modern print use Prophet there. The selected wording is retained. The final feet clause does not add ankles from another report.

segments.arabic: [190] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر أنه قال:
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

segments.arabic: كان الرجال والنساء يتوضؤون في زمان رسول الله ﷺ جميعا
segments.english: Men and women used to perform ablution together in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: [191] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن محمد بن المنكدر قال: سمعت جابرا يقول
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say:

segments.arabic: جاء رسول الله ﷺ يعودني وأنا مريض لا أعقل فتوضأ وصب علي من وضوئه فعقلت: فقلت: يا رسول الله لمن الميراث إنما يرثني كلالة فنزلت آية الفرائض
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to visit me while I was ill and not conscious. He performed ablution and poured some of the water from his ablution over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: “Messenger of Allah, to whom does the inheritance go? Only collateral relatives inherit from me.” Then the verse of the prescribed inheritance shares was revealed.

notes: The full chain, illness and loss of consciousness, water being poured, recovery, inheritance question and closing revelation statement remain. Kalalah is rendered collateral relatives here; this is a working lexical choice, not an inheritance ruling.

The selected source says one verse of the prescribed shares and gives no verse number. The plural in the Khan-family comparison and the explicit verse reference in Bewley are not inserted. The wording is poured, without changing it to sprinkled.

segments.arabic: [192] حدثنا عبد الله بن منير سمع عبد الله بن بكر قال: حدثنا حميد عن أنس قال
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Munir related to us; he heard ‘Abdullah ibn Bakr, who said: Humayd related to us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: حضرت الصلاة فقام من كان قريب الدار إلى أهله وبقي قوم فأتي رسول الله ﷺ بمخضب من حجارة فيه ماء فصغر المخضب أن يبسط فيه كفه فتوضأ القوم كلهم
segments.english: The time for prayer arrived. Those whose homes were near went to their families, and some people remained. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought a stone washbasin containing water. The washbasin was too small for him to spread his palm in it. All the people performed ablution.

segments.arabic: قلنا كم كنتم قال ثمانين وزيادة
segments.english: We asked: “How many were you?” He said: “Eighty and more.”

notes: The chain names Humayd in the selected Arabic and both prints; the Bewley page names Hammad here. The Arabic name is retained. The closing question and response remain a separate transmission segment.

The vessel is stone, without the English EPUB’s extra painted/stove wording or miracle comment. The answer says eighty and more, rather than changing the source’s conjunction to or. The source does not expressly state an additional hand-placement action here.

segments.arabic: [193] حدثنا محمد بن العلاء قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن بريد عن أبي بردة عن أبي موسى
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-‘Ala’ related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ دعا بقدح فيه ماء فغسل يديه ووجهه فيه ومج فيه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a cup containing water. He washed his hands and face in it and expelled water from his mouth into it.

notes: The complete chain and all three actions are retained. Water is made explicit as the object expelled from the mouth, matching the cup context and both English comparisons; no additional instruction from selected 185 is inserted.

segments.arabic: [194] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن أبي سلمة قال: حدثنا عمرو بن يحيى عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن زيد قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Salamah related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to us, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd, who said:

segments.arabic: أتى رسول الله ﷺ فأخرجنا له ماء في تور من صفر فتوضأ فغسل وجهه ثلاثا ويديه مرتين مرتين ومسح برأسه فأقبل به وأدبر وغسل رجليه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, and we brought out water for him in a brass basin. He performed ablution: he washed his face three times, each of his hands twice, wiped his head forward and back, and washed his feet.

notes: This entry and 195 share one original source paragraph. Their individually mapped spans and original paragraph remain traceable; they are not merged.

The historical print says أتانا (came to us), while the selected source and modern print have أتى (came). The selected form remains. No elbow or ankle limit is added from the English EPUB or neighbouring reports. Each hand is washed twice.

segments.arabic: [195] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة أن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: لما ثقل النبي ﷺ واشتد به وجعه استأذن أزواجه في أن يمرض في بيتي فأذن له فخرج النبي ﷺ بين رجلين تخط رجلاه في الأرض بين عباس ورجل آخر
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill and his pain intensified, he asked his wives for permission to be nursed in my house. They gave him permission. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out between two men, his feet dragging on the ground, between ‘Abbas and another man.

segments.arabic: قال عبيد الله فأخبرت عبد الله بن عباس، فقال أتدري من الرجل الآخر قلت لا قال هو علي
segments.english: ‘Ubaydullah said: I informed ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, and he said: “Do you know who the other man was?” I said: “No.” He said: “It was ‘Ali.”

segments.arabic: وكانت عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها تحدث أن النبي ﷺ قال: بعد ما دخل بيته واشتد وجعه هريقوا علي من سبع قرب لم تحلل أوكيتهن لعلي أعهد إلى الناس وأجلس في مخضب لحفصة زوج النبي ﷺ ثم طفقنا نصب عليه تلك حتى طفق يشير إلينا أن قد فعلتن ثم خرج إلى الناس
segments.english: And ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, used to relate that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, after he entered his house and his pain intensified: “Pour over me from seven waterskins whose ties have not been undone, so that I may give instructions to the people.” He was seated in a washbasin belonging to Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Then we began pouring those over him until he began indicating to us that we had done it. Then he went out to the people.

notes: The full account, ‘Ubaydullah’s intervening conversation and the resumed ‘A’ishah account remain in source order. The second account retains the selected pronoun his house, rather than substituting my house from the comparison translations.

The seven waterskins and their still-tied openings remain explicit. No seven-wells explanation or brass material is added. The selected honourific for ‘A’ishah is fully spoken in English. The historical print supplies ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib; the selected and modern form has only ‘Ali, which is retained.

segments.arabic: [196] حدثنا خالد بن مخلد قال: حدثنا سليمان قال: حدثني عمرو بن يحيى عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. He said: Sulayman related to us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Yahya related to me, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: كان عمي يكثر من الوضوء قال لعبد الله بن زيد أخبرني كيف رأيت النبي ﷺ يتوضأ فدعا بتور من ماء فكفأ على يديه فغسلهما ثلاث مرار ثم أدخل يده في التور فمضمض واستنثر ثلاث مرات من غرفة واحدة ثم أدخل يده فاغترف بها فغسل وجهه ثلاث مرات ثم غسل يديه إلى المرفقين مرتين مرتين ثم أخذ بيده ماء فمسح رأسه فأدبر به وأقبل ثم غسل رجليه، فقال هكذا رأيت النبي ﷺ يتوضأ
segments.english: My uncle used to perform ablution a great deal. He said to ‘Abdullah ibn Zayd: “Tell me how you saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.” He called for a basin of water, poured it onto his hands and washed them three times. Then he put his hand into the basin, rinsed his mouth and expelled water from his nose three times from one handful. Then he put his hand in, scooped up water with it and washed his face three times. Then he washed each of his hands up to the elbows twice. Then he took water with his hand and wiped his head backward and forward. Then he washed his feet and said: “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform ablution.”

notes: The opening يكثر من الوضوء is rendered a great deal without adding the word water. The comparison translations understand this as lavish or excessive ablution; the selected Arabic does not expressly name water in this clause. This wording decision remains open to independent English review. The source says expelling water from the nose; the extra inhalation verb in comparisons is not inserted.

The backward-then-forward order is retained, without substituting another report’s order. The selected and modern print use his hand in the singular for taking water before wiping; the historical print has both hands. No earthenware material, ankle limit or once-only count absent from this form is inserted.

segments.arabic: [197] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا حماد عن ثابت عن أنس
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from Thabit, from Anas:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ دعا بإناء من ماء فأتي بقدح رحراح فيه شيء من ماء فوضع أصابعه فيه قال أنس فجعلت أنظر إلى الماء ينبع من بين أصابعه قال أنس فحزرت من توضأ ما بين السبعين إلى الثمانين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, called for a vessel of water. A wide, shallow cup with some water in it was brought to him, and he put his fingers into it. Anas said: I began watching the water springing from between his fingers. Anas said: I estimated that those who performed ablution numbered between seventy and eighty.

notes: The wide shallow vessel, some water, between the fingers and estimated seventy-to-eighty count remain. The two repeated introductions Anas said are preserved; this stays separate from the earlier eighty-and-more report.

segments.arabic: [199] حدثنا أصبغ بن الفرج المصري عن ابن وهب قال: حدثني عمرو حدثني أبو النضر عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عبد الله بن عمر عن سعد بن أبي وقاص عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Asbagh ibn al-Faraj al-Misri related to us, from Ibn Wahb, who said: ‘Amr related to me; Abu al-Nadr related to me, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, from Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic: أنه مسح على الخفين وأن عبد الله بن عمر سأل عمر عن ذلك، فقال: نعم إذا حدثك شيئا سعد عن النبي ﷺ فلا تسأل عنه غيره،
segments.english: He wiped over his leather socks. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar asked ‘Umar about that, and he said: “Yes. When Sa‘d relates something to you from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do not ask anyone else about it.”

segments.arabic: وقال موسى بن عقبة أخبرني أبو النضر أن أبا سلمة أخبره أن سعدا، فقال عمر لعبد الله نحوه
segments.english: And Musa ibn ‘Uqbah said: Abu al-Nadr informed me that Abu Salamah informed him that Sa‘d ... Then ‘Umar said to ‘Abdullah something similar.

segments.arabic: [200] حدثنا عمرو بن خالد الحراني قال: حدثنا الليث عن يحيى بن سعيد عن سعد بن إبراهيم عن نافع بن جبير عن عروة بن المغيرة عن أبيه المغيرة بن شعبة عن رسول الله ﷺ

He said: Al-Layth related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Nafi‘ ibn Jubayr, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughirah, from his father al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

segments.arabic: أنه خرج لحاجته فاتبعه المغيرة بإداوة فيها ماء فصب عليه حين فرغ من حاجته فتوضأ ومسح على الخفين
segments.english: He went out to relieve himself. Al-Mughirah followed him with a small vessel containing water and poured water for him when he had finished relieving himself. He performed ablution and wiped over his leather socks.

segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Zakariyya related to us, from ‘Amir, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Mughirah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: كنت مع النبي ﷺ في سفر فأهويت لأنزع خفيه، فقال دعهما فإني أدخلتهما طاهرتين فمسح عليهما

segments.arabic: [206] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن يحيى بن سعيد عن بشير بن يسار مولى بني حارثة أن سويد بن النعمان أخبره

segments.arabic: [213] حدثنا عثمان قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قال
segments.english: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ بحائط من حيطان المدينة أو مكة فسمع صوت إنسانين يعذبان في قبورهما، فقال النبي ﷺ يعذبان وما يعذبان في كبير، ثم قال بلى كان أحدهما لا يستتر من بوله وكان الآخر يمشي بالنميمة ثم دعا بجريدة فكسرها كسرتين فوضع على كل قبر منهما كسرة فقيل له يا رسول الله لم فعلت هذا قال لعله أن يخفف عنهما ما لم تيبسا أو إلى أن ييبسا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed by a garden among the gardens of Madinah or Makkah. He heard the voices of two people being punished in their graves. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for something great.” Then he said: “Yes. One of them did not guard himself from his urine, and the other used to go about carrying tales.” Then he called for a palm stalk, broke it into two pieces, and placed a piece on each of their graves. He was asked: “Messenger of Allah, why did you do this?” He said: “Perhaps their punishment will be lightened as long as the two do not dry out—or until they dry out.”

notes: The selected Madinah-or-Makkah order remains; the historical print reverses the cities. Both final drying-time alternatives remain. The selected palm stalk has no added fresh/green adjective here.

segments.arabic: مر النبي ﷺ بقبرين، فقال إنهما ليعذبان وما يعذبان في كبير أما أحدهما فكان لا يستتر من البول وأما الآخر فكان يمشي بالنميمة ثم أخذ جريدة رطبة فشقها نصفين فغرز في كل قبر واحدة قالوا يا رسول الله لم فعلت هذا قال لعله يخفف عنهما ما لم ييبسا

One of them did not guard himself from urine, and the other used to go about carrying tales.” Then he took a fresh palm stalk, split it into two halves, and planted one in each grave. segments.english: She brought a young son of hers who had not yet eaten food to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, seated him in his lap, and he urinated on his garment. He called for water and sprinkled it, without washing it.

notes: The third-person report, son not yet eating food, lap, garment, sprinkling and not washing remain. The English comparisons differ in describing the application of water; the working translation retains the distinct source verbs rather than merging sprinkling and washing. No feeding age or legal rule is added.

segments.arabic: [222] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الأعمش عن أبي وائل عن حذيفة قال
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

segments.arabic: أتى النبي ﷺ سباطة قوم فبال قائما ثم دعا بماء فجئته بماء فتوضأ
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s refuse heap and urinated while standing. Then he called for water. I brought him water, and he performed ablution.

notes: Standing, the request for water, first-person response and ablution remain, with the full chain. No explanation of necessity or general permission is inserted.
