segments.arabic: [223] حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن أبي وائل عن حذيفة قال:
segments.english: ‘Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, from Hudhayfah, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيتني أنا والنبي ﷺ نتماشى فأتى سباطة قوم خلف حائط فقام كما يقوم أحدكم فبال فانتبذت منه فأشار إلي فجئته فقمت عند عقبه حتى فرغ
segments.english: I found myself walking with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He came to a people’s refuse heap behind a wall, stood as one of you stands, and urinated. I moved away from him, but he beckoned to me. I came to him and stood at his heel until he had finished.

notes: The shared walk, wall, standing comparison, moving away, beckoning and waiting remain. At his heel preserves the selected expression; no additional screening purpose from the chapter heading is inserted into the report.

segments.arabic: [224] حدثنا محمد بن عرعرة قال: حدثنا شعبة عن منصور عن أبي وائل قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn ‘Ar‘arah related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Mansur, from Abu Wa’il, who said:

segments.arabic: كان أبو موسى الأشعري يشدد في البول ويقول إن بني إسرائيل كان إذا أصاب ثوب أحدهم قرضه، فقال حذيفة ليته أمسك أتى رسول الله ﷺ سباطة قوم فبال قائما
segments.english: Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari used to be strict about urine. He would say: “Among the Children of Israel, when urine got onto someone’s garment, he would cut it out.” Hudhayfah said: “I wish he would refrain. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to a people’s refuse heap and urinated while standing.”

notes: The narrator’s account of Abu Musa and Hudhayfah’s response remain complete. The urine object follows the source context; no additional garment-cleaning procedure or legal commentary from the comparison footnote is included.

segments.arabic: [225] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال: حدثنا يحيى عن هشام قال: حدثتني فاطمة عن أسماء قالت
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: Fatimah related to me, from Asma’, who said:

segments.arabic: جاءت امرأة النبي ﷺ فقالت أرأيت إحدانا تحيض في الثوب كيف تصنع قال تحته ثم تقرصه بالماء وتنضحه وتصلي فيه
segments.english: A woman came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Tell me, when one of us menstruates in a garment, what should she do?” He said: “She should scrape it off, then rub it with water and sprinkle it, and pray in it.”

notes: The full chain and sequence of scraping, rubbing with water, sprinkling and praying remain. No extra washing procedure or legal explanation is inserted. The source question concerns menstruation in a garment; explanatory blood wording in the comparisons is not added as a separate clause.

segments.arabic: [226] حدثنا محمد قال: حدثنا أبو معاوية حدثنا هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us. Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: جاءت فاطمة بنت أبي حبيش إلى النبي ﷺ فقالت: يا رسول الله إني امرأة أستحاض فلا أطهر أفأدع الصلاة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لا إنما ذلك عرق وليس بحيض فإذا أقبلت حيضتك فدعي الصلاة وإذا أدبرت فاغسلي عنك الدم ثم صلي
segments.english: Fatimah bint Abi Hubaysh came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, I am a woman who has persistent bleeding and does not become pure. Should I leave the prayer?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “No. That is only a blood vessel, not menstruation. When your menstruation comes, leave the prayer, and when it ends, wash the blood off yourself, then pray.”

segments.arabic: قال، وقال أبي ثم توضأ لكل صلاة حتى يجيء ذلك الوقت
segments.english: He said: And my father said: “Then perform ablution for every prayer until that time comes.”

notes: The closing He said: And my father said is a separate transmission note. The working English does not insert the EPUB parenthetical attributing that addition directly to the Prophet. Hisham and his father remain in the full chain.

segments.arabic: [227] حدثنا عبدان قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا عمرو بن ميمون الجزري عن سليمان بن يسار عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: ‘Amr ibn Maymun al-Jazari informed us, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.english: I used to wash the semen from the garment of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would go out to the prayer while patches of water were still on his garment.

segments.arabic: [231] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن أنس قال
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: قدم أناس من عكل أو عرينة فاجتووا المدينة فأمرهم النبي ﷺ بلقاح وأن يشربوا من أبوالها وألبانها فانطلقوا فلما صحوا قتلوا راعي النبي ﷺ واستاقوا النعم فجاء الخبر في أول النهار فبعث في آثارهم فلما ارتفع النهار جيء بهم فأمر فقطع أيديهم وأرجلهم وسمرت أعينهم وألقوا في الحرة يستسقون فلا يسقون
segments.english: Some people from ‘Ukl or ‘Uraynah came and found Madinah unhealthy. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, directed them to camels giving milk and to drink their urine and milk. They went, and when they recovered, they killed the herdsman of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and drove away the livestock. The news came at the beginning of the day, and he sent after them. When the day had advanced, they were brought. He gave the order, and their hands and feet were cut off, their eyes were pierced with nails, and they were cast into al-Harrah. They asked for water but were not given any.

segments.arabic: قال أبو قلابة فهؤلاء سرقوا وقتلوا وكفروا بعد إيمانهم وحاربوا الله ورسوله
segments.english: Abu Qilabah said: “These people stole, killed, disbelieved after their belief, and waged war against Allah and His Messenger.”

notes: The ‘Ukl-or-‘Uraynah uncertainty, urine-before-milk order, recovery, killing, livestock, pursuit, timing, punishment and request for water remain. segments.arabic: [237] حدثنا عبدان قال: أخبرني أبي عن شعبة عن أبي إسحاق عن عمرو بن ميمون عن عبد الله قال

segments.english: While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was prostrating…

segments.arabic: ح قال وحدثني أحمد بن عثمان قال: حدثنا شريح بن مسلمة قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن يوسف عن أبيه عن أبي إسحاق قال: حدثني عمرو بن ميمون أن عبد الله بن مسعود حدثه

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان يصلي عند البيت وأبو جهل وأصحاب له جلوس إذ قال بعضهم لبعض أيكم يجيء بسلى جزور بني فلان فيضعه على ظهر محمد إذا سجد فانبعث أشقى القوم فجاء به فنظر حتى سجد النبي ﷺ وضعه على ظهره بين كتفيه وأنا أنظر لا أغير شيئا لو كان لي منعة قال: فجعلوا يضحكون ويحيل بعضهم على بعض ورسول الله ﷺ ساجد لا يرفع رأسه حتى جاءته فاطمة فطرحت عن ظهره فرفع رأسه، ثم قال اللهم عليك بقريش ثلاث مرات فشق عليهم إذ دعا عليهم قال: وكانوا يرون أن الدعوة في ذلك البلد مستجابة ثم سمى اللهم عليك بأبي جهل وعليك بعتبة بن ربيعة وشيبة بن ربيعة والوليد بن عتبة وأمية بن خلف وعقبة بن أبي معيط وعد السابع فلم نحفظه قال: فوالذي نفسي بيده لقد رأيت الذين عد رسول الله ﷺ صرعى في القليب قليب بدر
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying at the House, while Abu Jahl and some companions of his were sitting there. Some said to others: “Which of you will bring the afterbirth of the camel of the people of so-and-so and put it on Muhammad’s back when he prostrates?” The most wretched of the people got up and brought it. He waited until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, then placed it on his back between his shoulders. I was watching, unable to change anything. If only I had had protection! He said: They began laughing and leaning on one another, while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained prostrating without raising his head, until Fatimah came to him and threw it off his back. He raised his head, then said: “O Allah, deal with Quraysh,” three times. It distressed them when he prayed against them. He said: They believed that supplication in that land was answered. Then he named them: “O Allah, deal with Abu Jahl, and deal with ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi‘ah, al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf and ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt.” He named a seventh, but we did not remember him. He said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, I saw those whom the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had named lying dead in the well—the well of Badr.

checkedBody: While Allah's Apostle was prostrating (as stated below).

segments.arabic: [238] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن حميد عن أنس قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: بزق النبي ﷺ في ثوبه
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spat into his garment.

segments.arabic: طوله بن أبي مريم قال: أخبرنا يحيى بن أيوب حدثني حميد قال: سمعت أنسا عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Ibn Abi Maryam related it at greater length. He said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us. Humayd related to me. He said: I heard Anas, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The full closing Ibn Abi Maryam–Yahya ibn Ayyub–Humayd chain remains, including the source statement that it was related at greater length. The modern print includes this closing material. The historical print additionally begins it with Abu ‘Abdullah said and has Yahya ibn Ayyub related to me where the selected source has Humayd related to me. These differences are not silently supplied.

The short main report does not add while praying. The longer chapter quotation remains separate Arabic context. The English EPUB omits the closing transmission; Bewley’s online rendering also shortens and differs in the narrator designation.

segments.arabic: [239] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان قال: حدثنا الزهري عن أبي سلمة عن عائشة عن النبي ﷺ قال:

segments.arabic: كل شراب أسكر فهو حرام

segments.arabic: [240] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا سفيان بن عيينة عن أبي حازم سمع سهل بن سعد الساعدي
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. He said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah informed us, from Abu Hazim, who heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi:

segments.arabic: وسأله الناس وما بيني وبينه أحد بأي شيء دووي جرح النبي ﷺ، فقال: ما بقي أحد أعلم به مني كان علي يجيء بترسه فيه ماء وفاطمة تغسل عن وجهه الدم فأخذ حصير فأحرق فحشي به جرحه
segments.english: The people asked him—and there was no one between me and him—what the wound of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had been treated with. He said: “No one remains who knows more about it than I do. ‘Ali used to bring his shield with water in it, and Fatimah would wash the blood from his face. A mat was taken and burned, and his wound was packed with it.”

notes: The narrator’s there was no one between me and him remains, as do the shield, water, Fatimah’s washing and the burned mat. No material specification such as straw or inferred modern treatment instruction is added.

segments.arabic: [241] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن غيلان بن جرير عن أبي بردة عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ghaylan ibn Jarir, from Abu Burdah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: أتيت النبي ﷺ فوجدته يستن بسواك بيده يقول أع أع والسواك في فيه كأنه يتهوع
segments.english: I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and found him cleaning his teeth with a siwak in his hand, saying: “‘A‘, ‘a‘,” with the siwak in his mouth, as though he were retching.

segments.arabic: [243] وقال عفان حدثنا صخر بن جويرية عن نافع عن ابن عمر أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: And ‘Affan said: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: أراني أتسوك بسواك فجاءني رجلان أحدهما أكبر من الآخر فناولت السواك الأصغر منهما فقيل لي كبر فدفعته إلى الأكبر منهما
segments.english: “I saw myself using a siwak. Two men came to me, one older than the other. I handed the siwak to the younger of them, but I was told: ‘Give precedence to the elder.’ So I handed it to the older of them.”

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله اختصره نعيم عن ابن المبارك عن أسامة عن نافع عن ابن عمر

segments.arabic: [244] حدثنا محمد بن مقاتل قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا سفيان عن منصور عن سعد بن عبيدة عن البراء بن عازب قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Muqatil related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah informed us. He said: Sufyan informed us, from Mansur, from Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubaydah, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا أتيت مضجعك فتوضأ وضوءك للصلاة ثم اضطجع على شقك الأيمن ثم قل اللهم أسلمت وجهي إليك وفوضت أمري إليك وألجأت ظهري إليك رغبة ورهبة إليك لا ملجأ ولا منجى منك إلا إليك اللهم آمنت بكتابك الذي أنزلت وبنبيك الذي أرسلت فإن مت من ليلتك فأنت على الفطرة واجعلهن آخر ما تتكلم به
segments.english: “When you go to your bed, perform ablution as you do for the prayer, then lie down on your right side. Then say: ‘O Allah, I have surrendered my face to You, entrusted my affair to You, and sought support for my back with You, in hope and fear of You. There is no refuge and no escape from You except to You. O Allah, I believe in Your Book which You sent down, and in Your Prophet whom You sent.’ If you die that night, you will be upon the natural disposition. Make these the last words you speak.”

segments.arabic: قال: فرددتها علي النبي ﷺ فلما بلغت اللهم آمنت بكتابك الذي أنزلت قلت: ورسولك قال لا ونبيك الذي أرسلت
segments.english: He said: I repeated them to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. When I reached “O Allah, I believe in Your Book which You sent down,” I said: “And Your Messenger.” He said: “No: ‘And Your Prophet whom You sent.’”

notes: Face, entrusted affair, back, hope and fear, refuge and escape, Book and Prophet remain in the supplication. The natural disposition translates fitrah without inserting the comparison’s explanatory Islam parenthetical. The final correction from Messenger to Prophet remains in full.

The selected second O Allah before I believe remains; it is present in the modern print but absent at that point in the historical print. The second-person night-time condition and last-words instruction remain. No repeated phrase or honorific is shortened.
